Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Suggest how you would use a longitudinal study to investigate whether a person’s preferred
learning style changes over time.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe Kolb’s learning styles.

text: Kolb (1976) suggests a person prefers to learn using one of four learning styles. Perhaps this
preferred learning style is used only for A Levels or maybe it continues throughout life.

parts.text: Suggest how you would test the effectiveness of your new technique.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one explanation of learned helplessness. 
Psychology and Health
Section A
Answer this question.

text: You have devised a new technique, the CAT (Change in Attribution Technique), which will allow
people to change their negative attributions. You decide to see if the CAT works.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Explain, in your own words, what is meant by a ‘repeat prescription’ in relation to adherence
to medical requests.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one study which has measured non-adherence to medical requests using repeat
prescriptions. 
Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe what psychologists have found out about the patient-practitioner relationship.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have found out about the patient-practitioner relationship and
include a discussion about individual differences. 
Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Suggest how you would test whether the proposed measure of pain is both reliable and valid.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe one psychometric measure of pain, such as the McGill Pain Questionnaire (MPQ).

text: Your hospital manager wants to use a new psychometric measure of pain he has devised. As a
psychologist you know that any measure must be both reliable and valid.

parts.text:
Suggest how you would conduct a study using a brain scanner to determine the areas of the
brain associated with stress.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one study which has measured stress physiologically and one study which has
measured stress psychologically. 
Psychology and Environment
Section A
Answer this question.

text: Much research is done using brain scanners to find out which parts of the brain are responsible for
particular functions (as in the core study by Maguire et al. on taxi drivers).

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain, in your own words, what is meant by the term ‘coping with the effects of crowding’.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one study showing how people can be helped to cope with the effects of crowding.

Section B
Answer this question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have learned about natural disaster and technological
catastrophe.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have learned about natural disaster and technological
catastrophe, including a discussion about the ethics of conducting studies which people think

Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Suggest how you would conduct a field experiment to investigate whether transportation
noise has a negative effect on the educational performance of children.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Describe one study which has investigated the negative effects of noise on the performance
of children.

text: Noise may have negative effects on the ability of children to learn.

parts.text:

Section A
Answer this question.

text: Cognitive maps have been investigated in both humans and animals.

Answer this question.

parts.text: Describe what psychologists have found out about phobias.

parts.text:

Section C
Answer one question.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Describe the characteristics of addiction.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Suggest how you would investigate whether a person is addicted to using the internet.

text: Griffiths suggests that people can be addicted to anything, including the internet or cell (mobile)
telephones, if they possess typical characteristics of addiction.

parts.text: Describe two psychological definitions of abnormality.

Section A
Answer this question.

text: According to psychologists there are many definitions of abnormality, but these may be different
from how the general public define abnormality.
